messages:
Amy (Sales): Heads up — VividPay (Dedicated) reporting a big QoS regression after last runtime deploy. p95 chat latency jumped and they're seeing throttling. Customer wants ETA to fix.
Oncall Bot: New incident created: INC-1968504321 - VividPay p95 surge on dedicated pool.
Jordan Kim: pinging @eng-runtime + @product. Amy can you paste the customer payload/config and which pool/model?
Amy (Sales): Paste from customer: 'model: gpt-large-ql4, dedicated_pool: us-west-2-ded-3, started ~2026-03-19 22:10 UTC. Traffic ~350 r/s, avg seq ~512. Observed p95 3.4s (was ~0.9s).' They've attached flamegraphs and traces — I'll DM links.
Samir Patel: Thx. Early hypothesis: KV cache miss-rate spike or a batching fallback after the deploy. Need serving config (batch thresholds, cache config) and trace ids to pin.
Jordan Kim: Quick metric queries to run in console: 
```
rate(requests_total[5m]) by (pool)
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, pool))
```
Run and paste output.
Elaine Ryu: From product — this is a Dedicated customer with SLA. If it's a regression from the runtime change, we should treat as high priority. Marta, can you advise on priority and acceptable mitigations?
Marta Li: Need concise impact + rollback plan before calling P0. Questions: can we route VividPay to a previous runtime build or scale the pool temporarily? Acceptance criteria we want: p95 < 1.2s for 30m and no unexplained token-cost spike.
Samir Patel: Short-term mitigations I can try now: 1) route the pool to pre-deploy runtime image (we still have v2026-03-19-rc2), 2) enable fallback to tighter batching thresholds, 3) enforce truncation for long sequences (but that may change outputs). Amy — customer ok with routing?
Amy (Sales): Customer confirmed they prefer routing over any output-changing config. They accept temporary routing if we keep them updated.
Samir Patel: Doing routing -> rolled pool us-west-2-ded-3 to runtime v2026-03-19-rc2. Monitoring now.
Oncall Bot: rollout event recorded: rollout_id=rt-9087 by Samir.
Jordan Kim: If routing restores QoS within 15-20m, we capture root cause post-mitigation and scope fix for next sprint. If not, escalate to infra and runtime kernel leads.
Marta Li: Agreed. Please open a backlog ticket with impact, repro steps, owner, and attach traces. Proposed scope: focus on runtime/serving fixes (not model changes). Tentative triage: P1 if routing holds, P0 if not. Acceptance criteria for permanent fix: repro + fix + regression test + 48h stability.
Samir Patel: Update — p95 dropped to ~1.1s after routing, token cost normalized. Keeping watch for 60m and collecting traces. Creating bug RD-3581 now.
Amy (Sales): Notified customer: 'We routed you to a stable runtime build; monitoring shows p95 returned to normal. We'll follow up with a permanent plan and ETA.' Customer replied: thanks, wants ETA for permanent fix.
Marta Li: For roadmap: reproduce in staging with similar QPS/seq distribution, add KV-cache warmup/fallback and a cache-miss alert (delta >15%). Owners: Samir + Jordan. Target: ship in next sprint (~2 weeks).
Jordan Kim: Estimation: ~5 dev-days + 3 QA-days. I'll add RD-3581 to backlog with label customer-critical and link incident INC-1968504321. Any objections to timeline?
Elaine Ryu: :+1: no objections.
Oncall Bot: INC-1968504321 status -> mitigated (routing applied).
Marta Li: Next steps: Samir to attach traces + repro steps to RD-3581, Jordan to schedule staging run, Product to prioritize in next planning session. I'll own follow-up with customer for ETA.
Samir Patel: Will attach traces and a minimal repro script. Thanks everyone.
Jordan Kim: Closing loop — marking this thread for backlog handoff and adding to next planning agenda.
Amy (Sales): Thanks team — keeping customer updated.
